content: Posaconazole is a medication that can influence the metabolism of other drugs in your body. Specifically, it may slow down the elimination of certain drugs, potentially altering their effectiveness or increasing the risk of side effects. Similarly, other medications can affect how posaconazole is metabolized, which may impact its efficacy. In the event of an overdose, if the individual exhibits severe symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, immediately call emergency services (911). If the situation is less critical, contact a poison control center without delay. For residents in the United States, the poison control hotline is 1-800-222-1222. Before starting posaconazole, and periodically during treatment, laboratory tests should be conducted to monitor kidney and liver function, as well as blood mineral levels (e.g., calcium, magnesium, potassium). It is essential to attend all scheduled medical and laboratory appointments to ensure safe and effective use of the medication. If you miss a dose of posaconazole, it is crucial to consult your doctor or pharmacist promptly to establish a new dosing schedule. Do not attempt to double up on doses without professional guidance. For storage, refer to the product instructions or consult your pharmacist for specific details. Do not dispose of medications by flushing them down the toilet or pouring them into a drain unless explicitly instructed to do so. Properly discard the medication when it is expired or no longer needed, following local disposal regulations. This information is a summary and does not include all possible details about posaconazole. It does not guarantee that the medication is safe, effective, or appropriate for your specific condition. This document is not a substitute for professional medical advice. Always consult your healthcare provider for comprehensive information tailored to your health needs. Drug interactions are a critical consideration when using posaconazole. Keep a detailed list of all medications and supplements you are taking, including prescription, over-the-counter, and herbal products. Share this list with your doctor and pharmacist to minimize the risk of interactions and ensure optimal treatment outcomes. For any questions or concerns about posaconazole or its use, always seek advice from your healthcare professional.
